What to look for -- #3251, DXC issue triage
https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/3251

Every pane FAILS. That is the point: nothing here should be read as a diagnostic about the
shader, which is valid HLSL. Check the compiler's exit status and the "Output" pane, not the
(empty) assembly:

  dxc_1_6_2112   Program terminated with signal: SIGSEGV   (exit 139)
  dxc_trunk      Program terminated with signal: SIGSEGV   (exit 139)

dxc_trunk is a rolling build, so treat the exact shape as the class of failure rather than a
fixed signature; on Windows release binaries the same defect also appears as
"Internal compiler error: access violation", as UNREACHABLE in DataLayout::getTypeSizeInBits(),
and as "llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!". Every one of those is this bug.

The trigger is the whole-struct copy out of the implicit $Globals cbuffer into the
amplification payload: g_lhSampleData is a cbuffer-backed global, and
`p.lhSampleData = g_lhSampleData;` is emitted as one llvm.memcpy from that cbuffer.
TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy dispatches cbuffer-pointer users on HLOpcodeGroup and has no case
for HLOpcodeGroup::NotHL, which is what a plain llvm.memcpy is. Writing the same copy field by
field compiles cleanly -- that is the one-line difference.

LIMITATION, and it matters here. Compiler Explorer ships RELEASE builds, where DXC's asserts are
compiled out. The assert this issue is named for -- DXASSERT(0, "not implemented yet"),
lib/HLSL/HLOperationLower.cpp:8801 -- therefore CANNOT appear in any pane on this page. What you
see instead is what that unhandled case costs once the assert is gone: the untranslated memcpy is
left behind, the value it points at is deleted anyway, and something downstream dereferences it.
So CE corroborates the local Debug build here; it does not and cannot overrule it. The
authoritative measurement is a Debug build of main, which traps the assert itself.

No Clang pane: the repro is inherently an amplification shader (DispatchMesh + a payload), the
payload alloca is precisely what keeps the memcpy alive, and restating it as a compute shader
would exercise a different path and prove nothing.
